title: Lloyd Hundley, acetates and Tony's collection
summary: Roy recalls trombonist Lloyd Hundley and acetates made at his house, and the pair worry about Tony's failing health and what happens to his collection.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: No. Paul Baron was the director of the orchestra.... I mean, the producer of the show, Dick Tila(?), who finally committed suicide. He was a good friend of a trombone player of mine who was a very good player that didn't...he got killed in that accident with the Barnet(?) thing... Lloyd Hundley. You ever hear of him?
No.
Oh, he was good, man. You never heard of him!? A lot of musicians you didn't hear of that could play, eh.
Well, yeah. If they didn't get to make records or...
I think I've got some records of his that we made at my house on those acetates. Him and Shorty Sherock and myself. Tony's probably got all those things. Poor Tony, he's in bad shape now.
Is he?
Yeah.
Eldridge - 44
He was always too heavy.
Boy, he's gone. He's like a skeleton now. Like, when you lose weight when you're heavy like that, if you don't do no exercise, then all this becomes like fat... like on the elephant or something.
Yeah, it folds.
It starts to fold, you know.
I didn't know he was that sick.
Yes.
What is he going to do with all his stuff?
I don't know, man. He's sure got a lot of stuff, man. It's unfortunate, you know.
He's always held onto it. He hasn't given it to anybody to put it on a record or stuff like that.
Yeah.
But that should go to some archive or something. Does he have any close relatives or anything like that?
Yeah, I don't think they'd do... He's got a brother and sister.
I hope they know what it is. Because sometimes, if people don't know what it is, they throw it out.
Yeah. Well, he kept his stuff so immaculate and clean and good, you know.
[PAUSE]
